positive: The official Requirements adapter exposes a read-only existing-run contract resolver that accepts a project root and run ID, calls the package-owned frozen binding resolver, and derives every required Requirements rule reference from that validated immutable pack.

The adapter accepts bundled-v2 ready resolution and bounded legacy-v1 read-only resolution as distinct compatibility modes, with legacy fallback attempted only when the bundled binding is categorically missing rather than altered or incompatible.
Every returned rule path remains inside the validated resolved pack, exists as a regular non-symlink file, and contains the required official marker.
Selector changes, process working-directory changes, and caller-provided compatibility manifest values cannot affect this new existing-run resolver.
The existing pre-run stage_contract and public stage_request behavior remain unchanged for Phase 3 to migrate after provisioning and run binding are wired.

Focused proof covers bundled-v2 resolution, selector and cwd independence, categorical failures, bounded legacy continuation, rule inventory and marker validation, non-mutation, zero network access, and preservation of the current public route.
negative: Phase 2B.2 does not wire the new resolver into stage_request, task-start, Planning Lock, MCP, or any host projection and does not change the legacy public route before Phase 3 can create a frozen binding.

The new resolver never reads current.json, resolves relative to process cwd, accepts a caller manifest path, contacts the network, executes pack content, writes project state, provisions a pack, or creates or rewrites a run binding.

Missing, altered, stale, incompatible, conflicting, legacy-unauthorized, or unsafe state fails closed without falling back to another pack; only a categorically missing bundled binding may attempt the package resolver's bounded legacy continuation.
This slice does not edit tailtrail/aidlc_bundle.py, scripts/aidlc-official-bridge.py, scripts/planning_lock.py, scripts/task-start.py, schemas, package registration, CLI dispatch, or documentation.
